sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简讯栏目

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于 11 月 18 日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费阅读权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Hi, the news anchors all start by saying, our greatest responsibility is to serve our communities.
sentences.zh: 嗨，新闻主播们开场时总是说，我们最大的责任是服务我们的社区。

sentences.en: But what they are forced to say next has drawn attention to local news stations and who they are actually being asked to serve.
sentences.zh: 但他们接下来被迫说的话，却将人们的目光吸引到了地方新闻台身上，以及他们究竟被要求去服务谁。

sentences.en: It's Friday, April 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 4 月 6 日，星期五。

sentences.en: News at 10.
sentences.zh: 十点新闻。

sentences.en: A complete report with Patty Weiss and Bob Richardson.
sentences.zh: 由帕蒂·韦斯和鲍勃·理查森为您带来完整报道。

sentences.en: Michael Goodrich with the weather.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·古德里奇播报天气。

sentences.en: Ron Brooks on sports.
sentences.zh: 罗恩·布鲁克斯播报体育。

sentences.en: And the Eyewitness News team.
sentences.zh: 还有目击者新闻团队。

sentences.en: Hello there.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Here's what's happening at 10.
sentences.zh: 以下是十点新闻播报的内容。

sentences.en: For Arizonans, Decision 80 is just eight hours away.
sentences.zh: 对亚利桑那州人来说，“80年抉择”仅在八小时之后。

sentences.en: She was an anchor.
sentences.zh: 她是一名主播。

sentences.en: She was the first female evening anchor in the state of Arizona.
sentences.zh: 她是亚利桑那州第一位女性晚间新闻主播。

sentences.en: It'll be a busy day with voters choosing a president, a congressman, a senator, and various local offices, such as supervisor, assessor.
sentences.zh: 这将是忙碌的一天，选民们将选择总统、国会议员、参议员以及各种地方职务，例如监事、估税员。

sentences.en: Tucson is a place that she moved to when she was a child.
sentences.zh: 图森是她童年时搬去的地方。

sentences.en: Went off to San Diego for a couple years, but she moved back, became an evening anchor.
sentences.zh: 在圣迭戈待了几年后，她又搬了回来，成为了一名晚间主播。

sentences.en: A couple years after that, I was born.
sentences.zh: 几年后，我出生了。

sentences.en: I've seen video of it, a news hit and a story that ran the day I was born, when they sent a camera over to visit my mom in the hospital room.
sentences.zh: 我见过当时的录像，那是一则在我出生当天播出的新闻花絮和报道，当时他们派了一台摄像机去医院病房探望我妈妈。

sentences.en: So were you essentially brought into this world on TV?
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上是在电视上来到这个世界的？

sentences.en: I mean, the camera wasn't there as I was being born.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我出生的时候摄像机并不在场。

sentences.en: It was there, you know, a couple hours after.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它是在几个小时后才到那里的。

sentences.en: Aaron Weiss worked in local news for 14 years.
sentences.zh: 亚伦·韦斯在地方新闻行业工作了 14 年。

sentences.en: I went off to college and wanted nothing to do with journalism.
sentences.zh: 我上大学时对新闻业毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: I majored in theater.
sentences.zh: 我的主修专业是戏剧。

sentences.en: And after college, I went off to Microsoft and did the tech thing for a couple years.
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后，我去了微软，搞了几年技术。

sentences.en: And it was only after I'd been there for about a year that I realized I was missing that instant gratification.
sentences.zh: 直到在那儿工作大约一年后，我才意识到自己怀念那种即时的满足感。

sentences.en: So I took a week off and went back home to Tucson and hung out at the station for a week and wrote some stories and went out on a drug bust and proved I could do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我请了一周假，回老家图森待了一周，在电视台晃悠，写了些故事，还跟着去了一场打击毒品的行动，证明了自己能胜任。

sentences.en: And so they hired me as a producer.
sentences.zh: 于是他们雇我当了制作人。

sentences.en: So you started to work in the newsroom where your mother was an anchor?
sentences.zh: 所以你开始在你母亲担任主播的新闻编辑室工作？

sentences.en: I did, though I very rarely saw her.
sentences.zh: 是的，虽然我很少见到她。

sentences.en: Most of my time there, I was producing the morning show.
sentences.zh: 我在那里的绝大部分时间都在制作早间节目。

sentences.en: She was anchoring the six and the 10.
sentences.zh: 她则在主持六点档和十点档新闻。

sentences.en: So we would literally pass in the night.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真可以说是擦肩而过。

sentences.en: She'd be wrapping up the late show as I was showing up for the overnight shift.
sentences.zh: 当我赶来上夜班时，她正好结束了晚间节目的录制。

sentences.en: And how did you like the work?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这份工作怎么样？

sentences.en: I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: It's incredibly rewarding.
sentences.zh: 这非常有成就感。

sentences.en: You get to make something every day and see the results of what you do every day.
sentences.zh: 你每天都能创造出一些东西，并且每天都能看到自己劳动的成果。

sentences.en: And then you come in the next day and you've got a blank slate.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天你走进办公室，又是一张崭新的白纸。

sentences.en: And was there something about the fact that it was local news that made you take pride in it?
sentences.zh: 是因为这属于地方新闻，才让你对它产生了一种自豪感吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's that connection to a community.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那种与社区的联结感。

sentences.en: It's odd because local news is a very transient business.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪，因为地方新闻是一个流动性极强的行业。

sentences.en: It's very few folks stay in a market for years or decades.
sentences.zh: 很少有人能在某个市场待上好几年甚至几十年。

sentences.en: And the ones who do tend to be those trusted local anchors.
sentences.zh: 而那些留下来的人往往就是那些值得信赖的本地主播。

sentences.en: My mom could have played the TV news market game and left Tucson and picked up the family every couple of years, you know, from a Tucson to a Phoenix to a Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈本可以玩转电视新闻市场的游戏，离开图森，每隔几年就把全家迁往别处，你知道的，从图森到菲尼克斯再到洛杉矶。

sentences.en: To bigger and bigger markets, right?
sentences.zh: 去更大更大的市场，对吧？

sentences.en: But she didn't.
sentences.zh: 但她没有。

sentences.en: She chose to raise her family in Tucson because it was a sense of place.
sentences.zh: 她选择在图森把我们养大，因为这里有一种归属感。

sentences.en: And I will always be thankful to her for that.
sentences.zh: 我将永远为此对她心存感激。

sentences.en: Okay, folks.
sentences.zh: 好了，各位。

sentences.en: We'll be back tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: Good night, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家晚安。

sentences.en: We'll be on at 4.30 tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天四点半准时开播。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what was your first big break in the news biz?
sentences.zh: 那你进入新闻界获得的第一个重大机遇是什么？

sentences.en: So I was in Tucson for about a year and a half and decided to see what else was out there and ended up heading up to Portland, Oregon.
sentences.zh: 我在图森待了一年半左右，决定看看外面还有什么机会，最后去了俄勒冈州波特兰市。

sentences.en: So I took an associate producer position, bottom of the rung, pretty quickly worked my way up.
sentences.zh: 所以我接受了一个助理制作人的职位，也就是最底层的工作，但很快就晋升上去了。

sentences.en: And after spending my 20s in Portland, which is a great town to be single and in your 20s in, I got married, had a kid, and we decided it was time to head somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 在波特兰度过了我的二十多岁之后——那是个单身且正值二十多岁的好地方——我结婚了，有了孩子，我们觉得是时候去别的地方了。

sentences.en: So I started looking around for other positions and ended up getting offered a news director job in Sioux City, Iowa.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始寻找其他职位，最后获得了爱荷华州苏城的一个新闻总监职位。

sentences.en: And it was a big promotion for me at that point.
sentences.zh: 对当时的政客我来说，这是一次大晋升。

sentences.en: I'd been a manager on kind of a fill-in basis in
sentences.zh: 我在波特兰担任过类似代班性质的

sentences.en: Portland, getting to run the newsroom when folks weren't there.
sentences.zh: 管理者，在别人不在时负责运营新闻编辑室。

sentences.en: But getting my own newsroom, my own shop was a great opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但能拥有我自己的新闻编辑室、我自己的阵地，这是一个绝佳的机会。

sentences.en: So we packed up and moved to the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 于是我们收拾行李，搬到了中西部。

sentences.en: This is Siouxland News at Sunrise on KMAG 14.
sentences.zh: 这里是 KMAG 14 台的《苏兰早间新闻》。

sentences.en: Police say this man is passing counterfeit bills and they want your help catching him.
sentences.zh: 警方称此人一直在使用假钞，他们希望大家协助将其抓获。

sentences.en: And what was your vision as news director for running this TV station?
sentences.zh: 作为新闻总监，你对运营这家电视台有什么愿景？

sentences.en: For me, it was a chance to build something.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一个建立一番事业的机会。

sentences.en: It was a small, struggling station.
sentences.zh: 这是一是一家规模较小、举步维艰的电视台。

sentences.en: It came from an ownership group that had gone through a fairly spectacular bankruptcy a couple of years prior.
sentences.zh: 它的母公司在几年前经历了一次相当轰动的破产。

sentences.en: It was still basically being held by the bankruptcy court and the creditors.
sentences.zh: 它当时基本上仍然由破产法院和债权人在把持。

sentences.en: And you know in a market that size that you're going to be working with maybe a few veterans, but primarily new reporters.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，在那种规模的市场里，你共事的可能有一些资深老员工，但主要还是新记者。

sentences.en: And that to me was exciting.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So you knew going into this job that this was a small station, that it was financially struggling.
sentences.zh: 所以你在接手这份工作时，就知道这是一家小电视台，而且财务状况堪忧。

sentences.en: And it sounds like those two things were in some ways a draw for you because it meant that you had the ability to put your own imprint on it.
sentences.zh: 听起来在某些方面，这两点恰恰对你很有吸引力，因为这意味着你有能力在上面打上你自己的烙印。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It was that feeling of being a part of that place.
sentences.zh: 那就是成为那个地方一部分的感觉。

sentences.en: When did that feeling, which it sounds like this was going well and that you were enjoying this work, when did that feeling start to change?
sentences.zh: 这种感觉——听起来当时一切顺利，你也乐在其中——是什么时候开始改变的呢？

sentences.en: So after I'd been there for about a year and a half, we got word that Sinclair was looking at buying the station.
sentences.zh: 我在那里待了一年半左右后，我们接到消息称辛克莱尔有意收购这家电视台。

sentences.en: And these things take a couple months to close.
sentences.zh: 而这类交易通常需要几个月的时间才能完成。

sentences.en: Sinclair ended up officially buying the station in fall around October of 2013.
sentences.zh: 辛克莱尔最终于 2013 年秋天（大约 10 月份）正式完成了对该台的收购。

sentences.en: So Sinclair was founded in 1971 by the current chairman's father, Julian Sinclair Smith.
sentences.zh: 辛克莱尔由现任董事长之父朱利安·辛克莱尔·史密斯于 1971 年创立。
zh_words: 朱利安·辛克莱尔·史密斯

sentences.en: He was an electrical engineer with a deep curiosity about new broadcasting technology.
sentences.zh: 他是一名电气工程师，对新的广播技术有着浓厚的好奇心。

sentences.en: Sydney Ember is a media reporter for The Times.
sentences.zh: 悉尼·恩伯是《时报》的一名媒体记者。

sentences.en: And the company started off very small.
sentences.zh: 这家公司最初起步时规模非常小。

sentences.en: It was one radio station and one television station in Maryland, in Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 它在马里兰州巴尔的摩拥有一家广播电台和一家电视台。

sentences.en: But it wanted to get bigger.
sentences.zh: 但它想要做大。

sentences.en: And it started buying more and more stations, which coincided with this sort of deregulation that allowed companies to own more stations.
sentences.zh: 它开始收购越来越多的电视台，这恰好与当时允许公司拥有更多电视台的那种放松管制潮不谋而合。

sentences.en: We saw no reason, no harm to the public that would result from networks acquiring stations.
sentences.zh: 我们看不到网络收购电视台会给公众带来任何理由或危害。

sentences.en: And after all, the touchstone on this, it seems to me, ought not to be the interest of the Hollywood producers
sentences.zh: 毕竟在我看来，衡量此事的标准不应当是好莱坞制作人

sentences.en: or the networks or the group owners, but rather whether or not the viewers in particular markets are better off.
sentences.zh: 或电视网络或集团所有者的利益，而更应该是特定市场的观众是否因此过得更好。

sentences.en: And we believe they will be if we permit groups to be able to acquire other stations.
sentences.zh: 我们相信，如果我们允许集团收购其他电视台，他们就会过得更好。

sentences.en: And that doesn't mean that independently owned stations don't do very well.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着独立拥有的电视台就不能经营得很好。

sentences.en: They do do very well in markets, depending upon the owners and their management capabilities.
sentences.zh: 根据所有者及其管理能力，它们在各自市场上的确能经营得非常出色。

sentences.en: But there are, the economists tell us, some very good efficiencies that result when an entity is able to grow larger.
sentences.zh: 但经济学家告诉我们，当一个实体能够不断做大时，会产生非常好的规模效应。

sentences.en: And this oftentimes serves our people very well in our society.
sentences.zh: 这往往能很好地为我们社会中的人民服务。

sentences.en: And we ought not to lose sight of that.
sentences.zh: 我们不应忽视这一点。

sentences.en: So there might have been a time where a company could own a set number of stations.
sentences.zh: 所以过去可能曾有过一个时期，一家公司只能拥有固定数量的电视台。

sentences.en: There might have been a cap.
sentences.zh: 当时可能存在一个上限。

sentences.en: And suddenly there wasn't.
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，上限取消了。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: You know, for a long time, the cap was, I think, five.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很长一段时间里，上限好像是五个。

sentences.en: And then they moved it up to seven and then 12.
sentences.zh: 后来他们把它提高到七个，然后是十二个。

sentences.en: So suddenly it's possible for a company to own not just a handful of stations, but a very large number of local TV stations.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，一家公司不仅可以拥有少数几家电视台，还可以拥有数量非常庞大的地方电视台。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And by the early 2000s, Sinclair owned, you know, something like 60 stations across the country.
sentences.zh: 到 2000 年代初，辛克莱尔在全国范围内拥有大约 60 家电视台。

sentences.en: We knew the station was up for sale and someone was going to come in at some point and buy it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道电视台正在挂牌出售，总有一天会有人来买下它。

sentences.en: The fact that it was Sinclair looking at us was also not a surprise.
sentences.zh: 看中我们的是辛克莱尔，这一点其实也不让人意外。

sentences.en: And on paper seemed like a good thing because you've got a very large, well-resourced company coming in.
sentences.zh: 而且从纸面上看似乎是件好事，因为你将迎来一家规模庞大、资源雄厚的大公司。

sentences.en: And so the hope would be an owner like that comes in and starts giving you more reporters.
sentences.zh: 所以人们的期望是，像这样的一家所有者进驻后，会开始为你提供更多的记者。

sentences.en: You start adding newscasts, the sorts of things that you'd hope to see when a well-resourced company comes in to what had been a poorly resourced station.
sentences.zh: 你开始增加新闻节目，当你期望一家资源丰富公司入主一家原本资源匮乏的电视台时，你会希望看到这些改变。

sentences.en: And I'd hope they would have seen what we were doing there as something that had a lot of potential for growth.
sentences.zh: 我本希望他们能把我们在那里做的事情看作是极具发展潜力的事情。

sentences.en: So what happens at these stations that Sinclair is buying up?
sentences.zh: 那么，在辛克莱尔收购的这些电视台里究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: What changes about the actual day-to-day operations?
sentences.zh: 实际的日常运营发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: So sometimes these stations are happy to hear that a company like Sinclair is buying them
sentences.zh: 所以有时这些电视台很高兴听到像辛克莱尔这样的公司收购它们

sentences.en: because they'll now have resources to go out and report local news resources that they might not have had before Sinclair came in.
sentences.zh: 因为它们现在将拥有资源去进行地方新闻报道，这些资源可能是辛克莱尔进驻之前它们所不具备的。

sentences.en: But pretty quickly, these stations start to realize that things aren't as rosy as they seemed.
sentences.zh: 但很快，这些电视台开始意识到事情并没有表面上看起来那么美好。

sentences.en: So right around the time the sale is closing, I fly down to North Carolina for a meeting with news directors from other stations that had been recently acquired by Sinclair.
sentences.zh: 所以在收购接近完成的那个时间点，我飞往北卡罗来纳州，与辛克莱尔最近收购的其他电视台的新闻总监开会。

sentences.en: And we're all at the airport.
sentences.zh: 我们都在机场。

sentences.en: We get on a van on the way to the hotel and we're talking.
sentences.zh: 我们上了去酒店的厢型车，大家聊了起来。

sentences.en: And someone asks about must-run pieces.
sentences.zh: 有人问起了必播稿件的事。

sentences.en: So a must-run is a segment that is generally centrally produced that Sinclair asked its stations to run.
sentences.zh: 所以“必播稿件”是一个通常由总部制作、辛克莱尔要求其旗下电视台播出的节目片段。

sentences.en: It sends out these segments to its stations across the country and it says, run these during a specific period of time.

sentences.zh: 而每一个拥有家庭、拥有配偶、与他们生活了20年、30年或40年的社区有着联系的主播，

sentences.en: every single one of them was in that position.
sentences.zh: 他们每一个人都处在那个位置上。

sentences.en: And what does your mother think about all this?
sentences.zh: 你母亲对这一切怎么看？

sentences.en: Did she watch that video of all the Sinclair anchors saying the exact same thing?
sentences.zh: 她看过那段所有辛克莱主播都在说完全相同话的视频吗？

sentences.en: She saw it.
sentences.zh: 她看到了。

sentences.en: I'm sure she was as horrified as the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 我确信她和我们其他人一样感到震惊。

sentences.en: She's been out of the business for over 10 years now.
sentences.zh: 她离开这个行业已经有10多年了。

sentences.en: She lives in Seattle now.
sentences.zh: 她现在住在西雅图。

sentences.en: She gets Como, Sinclair Station up there, but she doesn't watch much.
sentences.zh: 她能看到西雅图的辛克莱电视台 Como 台，但她不怎么看。

sentences.en: And honestly, I don't think she watches much TV.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为她不怎么看电视。

sentences.en: And honestly, I don't watch much local TV anymore either.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我也不怎么看本地电视了。

sentences.en: We don't have cable anymore and where I live up in the mountains, you can't get anything over the air.
sentences.zh: 我们不再有有线电视了，在我住的山上，你用天线什么也收不到。

sentences.en: So occasionally I'll stream a local newscast on my phone if I'm feeling nostalgic, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我偶尔感到怀旧的话，我会在手机上播放本地新闻节目的流媒体。

sentences.en: But I guess in some ways I've moved on too.
sentences.zh: 但我想在某种程度上我也已经前进了。

sentences.en: Sounds like both of you, in a sense, have started to give up a bit on TV news.
sentences.zh: 听起来你们两个人在某种程度上都已经开始对电视新闻有点放弃了。

sentences.en: I think we have.
sentences.zh: 我想我们是这样的。

sentences.en: Well, Aaron, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚伦，非常感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Michael, it's been my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app, unlocked?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格管控的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了自称是改革派的一群人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》中，我是主持人莎拉·凯尼格，为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失控的故事。
